If possible, you could consider making a dish that's budget-friendly but still delicious and plentiful, such as a hearty stew, a big batch of cookies, or a fruit salad. You could also think about potluck-style dishes that can be made in large quantities without breaking the bank. Another option might be to talk to your mother about scaling back the amount of food you bring, while still contributing something to the celebration. Perhaps you could bring a smaller dish or a few dozen cookies instead of a large quantity of food. It's also worth considering reaching out to other community members to see if they can contribute to the celebration as well. That way, the burden of providing food isn't solely on your family, and everyone can enjoy the celebration together. Remember, the harvest celebration is about more than just the food – it's about coming together as a community and sharing in the joy of the season. I'm sure your family's contribution, no matter how big or small, will be appreciated and valued.
